profile.bio:
I am a Ph.D. candidate in Transportation and Supply Chain Management at North Dakota State University and a Graduate Research Assistant at the Upper Great Plains Transportation Institute (UGPTI), advised by Prof. Pan Lu.

My work sits where transportation research meets professional logistics practice. Before doctoral study I worked in freight forwarding, procurement, and logistics project management in China and Ghana. Today I develop decision-support solutions using multi-criteria decision-making, econometric modeling, machine learning, and geographic information systems.

My research spans autonomous freight systems, agricultural supply chains, transportation economics, supply chain resilience, digital logistics, and sustainable freight transportation.

projects.title: Autonomous Truck Adoption in Rural Agricultural Communities
projects.methods: Fuzzy AHP, FCB-FCM, Expert Survey, R, LaTeX, Multi-Stakeholder Analysis
projects.details:
Designed multi-stakeholder expert surveys for truck drivers, technology providers, government agencies, logistics specialists, and academics.
Applied a Fuzzy Cognitive Behavioral–Fuzzy AHP (FCB-FAHP) methodology to model causal links between adoption drivers and barriers.
Developed a Fuzzy Cognitive Mapping–based weighting scheme to prioritize the transformational dynamics of autonomous truck deployment.
Findings published in the Journal of Business Logistics (2026, 47(4), e70097).

projects.title: Hazardous Materials (HazMat) Freight Risk & Resilience Analysis
projects.methods: GIS, Risk Assessment, Spatial Analysis, Policy Frameworks
projects.details:
Investigated hazardous materials transportation risks across North Dakota's rural freight network.
Conducted spatial analysis of HazMat incident hotspots and evaluated regulatory policy effectiveness.
Integrated a multi-level perspective (MLP) framework to assess transition dynamics in HazMat logistics.

projects.title: Greenhouse Gas Emissions from Mobile Device Location Data
projects.methods: R, FRED API, ArcGIS, Quantile Regression, IV (2SLS), Log-Linear Modeling
projects.details:
Built a multi-layered econometric framework (seasonal log-linear, quantile regression, IV) to estimate gasoline price elasticity of VMT at census-tract level in the Washington, D.C. metro area.
Implemented 2SLS estimation with exogenous instruments (station density, crude oil prices, state tax rates).
Analyzed urban–rural distributional heterogeneity and seasonal differences in price responsiveness.
